findings.summary: A search engine is an application software that returns hyperlinks to web pages in response to user queries submitted via browser or mobile app. Its engine operates as part of a distributed computing system across global data centers, relying on a continuously updated indexing system driven by automated web crawlers. These crawlers mine files and databases on web servers, though some content remains in the deep web and inaccessible to crawlers. Market share is highly concentrated, with one provider holding approximately 89–90% of worldwide search share as of May 2025, while competitors trail far behind. Because of this dominance, website visibility improvements, known as search engine marketing and optimization, have historically focused heavily on that provider.

mechanisms.title: Indexing system
mechanisms.explanation: The engine's speed and accuracy depend on a complex system of indexing that is continuously updated by automated web crawlers. Crawlers mine files and databases on web servers to build the index, but some content is deep web and not accessible to crawlers.

mechanisms.title: Distributed computing engine
mechanisms.explanation: For a search provider, its engine is part of a distributed computing system that can encompass many data centers throughout the world. This infrastructure supports the processing of queries against the index.

unknowns: Exact algorithms used for ranking and relevance scoring
Internal mechanisms for handling deep web content exclusion
Details of crawler scheduling and freshness policies
Specific data center distribution and load-balancing strategies
